claims.sentence: To conduct ongoing and interim assessments for students with disabilities, adapted evaluation materials must be developed upon the submission of a written application
These materials must allow for the evaluation of the achievement of learning outcomes and the level of all competences’ development mentioned in the education program
The form of assessment is defined taking into account the peculiarities of mental and physical development
Options include verbal responses, written responses on paper, written responses on a computer, or a test format
For students with visual impairment, the University must provide an assistant to provide necessary assistance during pass fail exams and exams
Written exercises are dictated to an assistant
A technical assistive device must be provided for task completion if necessary, and the usage of own technical assistive devices is also possible
For students with serious health problems such as speech disorder, deafness, or hard of hearing, oral assessments must be held in a written form
Disabled students are entitled to additional time to prepare their answer during a test or an exam upon a written request and in case of necessity
The duration of an assessment session cannot be extended to more than 1.5 hours
Disabled students might use assistive devices during assessment sessions taking into consideration their special needs
The evidence does not specify the procedure or deadline for submitting the written application
The evidence does not specify the procedure for defining the form of assessment or determining the "peculiarities of mental and physical development"
The evidence does not specify how the assistant is selected or trained
The evidence does not specify the procedure for determining if a student has a "serious health problem" or which specific conditions qualify
The evidence does not specify the procedure for requesting additional time or how "necessity" is determined
The evidence does not specify which assistive devices are available or how they are provided
